story.title: Crypto Markets Today, November 15, 2026: Bitcoin Rebounds From $62,000 as Ethereum, Solana Slide - Eurasia Business News

facts.text: At 07:30 UTC on November 13, 2026, bitcoin traded at about $69,000, down a little over 6% in 24 hours, after touching an intraday low of $67,922 according to CoinGecko.
Based on CoinGlass data analysed by CoinDesk early Friday, more than $1.3 billion in crypto futures were liquidated within 24 hours, about $677 million of them on bitcoin.
Per Cointelegraph, data from 10x Research show bitcoin fell 5.9% between November 5 and 12, while the 10-year Treasury yield climbed above 5%.
Crypto news at a glance: bitcoin, ether, BNB and XRP this morning Losses run through the large caps, but not evenly.
The Crypto Fear and Greed Index from alternative.me reads 20 on Friday, which is "Extreme Fear", down from 28 the day before.

This crypto news roundup sets out what is driving the move: forced selling of leveraged positions, outflows from US spot bitcoin ETFs, a strong dollar with rising Treasury yields, and thin order books.
If you are asking why is crypto down today, our running explainer tracks every sell-off of the year.
For medium-term scenarios, see our bitcoin price prediction and ethereum price prediction.
By John Meyer, consultant in finance and business – Eurasia Business News, November 15, 2026.
Cryptocurrency markets remained under pressure Sunday, November 15, as Bitcoin recovered from a sharp overnight decline while Ethereum, Solana and other major digital assets struggled to stabilize.

Bitcoin briefly traded near $62,000 before recovering toward $65,000, gaining +0.66% over the day, reflecting a volatile market shaped by institutional withdrawals, forced liquidations and expectations of higher U.S. interest rates.
Investors will watch whether Bitcoin’s rebound survives renewed selling, whether ETF withdrawals moderate and whether leveraged liquidations subside.
Expectations surrounding the Federal Reserve’s December policy meeting remain another source of uncertainty.
Meanwhile, the Crypto Fear & Greed Index fell to 12 on November 15 , classified as extreme fear.
That reading describes sentiment rather than proving that prices have bottomed.
U.S. spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds recorded approximately $1.07 billion in net outflows during the latest trading week.
Bitcoin.com, citing SoSoValue, reported approximately $2.97 billion in withdrawals across 12 trading sessions ending November 13.
These are preceding trading-session flows, not Sunday ETF redemptions.
Bitcoin.com cited DefiLlama data showing approximately $284.85 billion outstanding on November 14, down 5.36% over 30 days.
Tether’s USDT and Circle’s USDC together accounted for $244.42 billion.
XRP attracted attention after falling below $1 and touching approximately $0.8922.
Eastern time, but the rebound followed prices last seen around November 2024.
The $1 threshold was psychologically important, although crossing it does not independently determine future direction.
Ethereum’s native asset, Ether, also experienced substantial volatility.
Investing.com reported an overnight low of $1,711 before a recovery toward $1,808 in its morning update.
The move left Ether below $2,000 despite a meaningful bounce from its weakest level.
